# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, since `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` landed, a bundled
build-time registry (the browser). There is no mechanism for hosting a pack
catalogue remotely, so publishing or updating a pack forces a rebuild and
re-release of the game. This item implements the **remote source provider** on
top of the pack-source registry abstraction (`PackSource[]` /
`PackSourceRegistry`) introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** — hosts a signed pack catalogue at a URL and
  expects packs to appear in players' Card Packs panels without rebuilding the
  game.
- **Main Street player** — experiences remote packs identically to bundled
  packs (lock → purchase → enable → deal) and continues to play offline on
  bundled packs when the remote host is unreachable.

Example user stories:

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack catalogue at a URL
> that the game verifies with a signed manifest, so I can publish or update
> packs for an installed game without rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want remote packs to appear in my Card Packs panel and behave
> exactly like bundled packs, while the game still boots and plays offline on
> bundled packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Locked design decisions (producer, 2026-10-17)

- **Q1 — Configuration: build-time config constant.** Remote source URLs are
  declared in a build-time config constant (e.g. an environment variable read
  by `vite.config.ts` / a config module), matching the bundled-source pattern.
  No runtime URL mutation in this iteration; launcher-supplied or well-known
  URLs are a possible follow-up.
- **Q2 — Integrity: signed manifests (Ed25519).** Remote manifests are signed
  (Ed25519); the game verifies the signature against a pinned public key before
  trusting any remote pack content. A manifest that fails verification is
  rejected whole (no packs from that source) with a logged warning — safe
  refusal, never a crash. Host allow-list remains as the first gate (only
  configured URLs are fetched at all).
- **Q3 — Timeout & degradation: bounded hard timeout, console-only warning.**
  A hard fetch timeout (≈3 s) bounds the boot path; on failure the game boots
  on bundled packs and logs a warning to the console. **No UI change** — no
  toast, no panel indicator. The Card Packs listing is never empty when a
  bundled pack exists.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence: bundled always wins.** When the same pack id
  appears in more than one source, the **bundled source wins**; a remote pack
  can never override bundled core content. This is implemented by keeping the
  bundled source registered *before* the remote source in the registry (the
  registry's first-wins consultation order) plus an explicit test asserting the
  precedence.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` (`createRemotePackSource`)
   that fetches a pack manifest and pack CSVs from a configured base URL via
   the loader's existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` transport seam and
   contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Declare remote source URLs as a build-time config
   constant (e.g. `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` or a config module), consumed when the
   default registry is built. Multiple remote sources compose additively in
   registration order, always **after** the bundled source.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Pack-id precedence is deterministic: bundled wins
   over remote (remote registered after bundled). Pack-id conflicts between two
   remote sources resolve first-wins (registration order). The core merge
   contract continues to reject duplicate card ids whole.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Remote packs are not
   automatically ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable, or serving a
   malformed manifest degrades to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never blocks boot, never blanks the listing. A bounded timeout (≈3 s) is
   applied to the manifest fetch (and per-file fetches).
6. **Trust and integrity.** Remote manifests are **Ed25519-signed**; the game
   verifies the signature against a pinned public key before trusting content.
   Failure modes: bad signature / missing signature / malformed manifest →
   reject source whole with a warning. Host allow-list: only configured URLs
   are fetched.
7. **Caching / offline.** No client-side caching of remote packs in this
   iteration — remote packs require the remote host at load time; the offline
   story is the bundled packs. Cache in `localStorage` / Cache Storage is a
   recorded follow-up.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, signed-manifest verification,
   degradation, gating, precedence and asset resolution with tests; document
   the remote-hosting contract (configuration, signing, hosting layout,
   degradation).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
   URL is fetched at runtime and its packs appear in the Card Packs panel
   alongside bundled packs.
2. **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
   lock → purchase → enable → deal flow, including save/load persistence.
3. **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
   malformed manifest, the game boots on bundled packs and logs a warning; the
   Card Packs listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists; the fetch is
   bounded by a timeout (≈3 s) so boot is never blocked.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
   header/duplicate id is rejected whole with a logged warning, without
   affecting packs from other sources.
5. **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
   with the same pack id; conflicts between remote sources resolve
   first-wins in registration order; precedence is explicit and tested.
6. **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
   missing, invalid, or not produced by the pinned key is rejected whole with a
   logged warning and no packs from that source are loaded; the failure mode is
   documented.
7. **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
   coordinated with `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained) — remote
   assets resolve through the environment-injected `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`
   seam.
8. **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
   remote configuration, the hosting contract (layout, signing), integrity and
   degradation.
9. **Testing.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes; remote
   discovery, signature verification, degradation, precedence, gating and asset
   resolution are covered by automated tests.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing seams.** The remote source consumes the existing injectable
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports on the loader
  (`createPackSourceTransports`); no core loader changes.
- **Totality.** The remote source never throws: network failures, timeouts,
  malformed responses, signature failures, and missing files all resolve to
  `null` and the core loader degrades to bundled/static packs.
- **Additive.** The remote source is added to the existing
  `PackSourceRegistry` **after** the bundled source, without modifying bundled
  or content-directory sources.
- **Bounded timeout.** Remote fetches on the boot path are bounded (≈3 s) so
  the game never stalls waiting for a slow or hung host.
- **Signing key separation.** The pinned verification public key is a build-time
  constant; the private signing key is held by the distribution operator and is
  never shipped in the game.
- **Pack content stays licence-clean.** Remote packs must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs (documented in the hosting contract).
- **No runtime URL mutation** in this iteration (build-time config only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, signature
  verification, registration and precedence.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source configuration + transport
  wiring (consumes the `packSources` option).
- `vite.config.ts` / config module (e.g. `src/mainStreetRemotePacks.ts`) —
  build-time remote URL + pinned public key declaration.
- `src/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — remote source boot wiring.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — transport usage (should not need changes).
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, signature verification, degradation,
  precedence, asset-resolution tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline or signing tooling UI (a natural follow-up
  — the signing key/algorithm contract is defined here, tooling later).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.
- Client-side caching of remote packs for offline use (recorded follow-up).
- Runtime/launcher-supplied remote URL mutation (build-time config only).

## Related work

- **`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`** — Make card packs available in the browser
  distribution: provides `PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry`; **blocks** this
  item (this item depends on it). Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`** — Make card-pack assets self-contained: pack art
  resolves from pack assets; remote assets must consume the
  `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` seam. Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`** — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import:
  parent context for the DLC channel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; a hostile pack could
  inject arbitrary card data. *Mitigation:* Ed25519-signed manifests verified
  against a pinned public key; host allow-list; safe refusal (reject whole,
  log warning, never crash).
- **Risk — signing overhead.** Key management, signing tooling, and
  verification bugs. *Mitigation:* verification is a small, isolated,
  well-tested function; private key never ships; the public key is pinned at
  build time; signing tooling can be a follow-up (the contract is defined).
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the
  game. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout (≈3 s), non-blocking degradation,
  bundled-first registry order.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack cannot
  use it offline. *Mitigation:* explicit decision — no remote caching this
  iteration; bundled packs remain the offline story; caching recorded as a
  follow-up.
- **Risk — scope creep.** Caching, signing tooling, runtime URL mutation, and a
  pack CDN are natural follow-ups. *Mitigation:* recorded as out of scope /
  linked follow-ups, not built here.
- **Assumption — registry seam exists.** `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` provides the
  `PackSource` abstraction; this item adds a provider rather than
  re-architecting.
- **Assumption — transport seams are adequate.** The existing
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports can serve a remote
  source without core changes.
- **Assumption — Ed25519 available.** A small Ed25519 verification
  implementation (e.g. WebCrypto `crypto.subtle`/`Ed25519`, or a tiny
  dependency) is available in the browser and test environments; the exact
  mechanism is an implementation detail the implementer records.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Configuration mechanism** (how remote source URLs are declared:
  build-time constant / launcher setting / well-known URL). — **Answer
  (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17): A — build-time config constant.**
  Matches the bundled-source pattern; simplest; runtime URL mutation is a
  recorded follow-up. Source: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q2 — Pack-integrity model** (host allow-list / allow-list + checksum /
  signed manifests). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17):
  C — signed manifests (Ed25519).** Verification against a pinned public key;
  failure rejects the source whole with a warning. Source: worklog comment
  `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q3 — Timeout and degradation behaviour** (hard timeout + console only /
  + toast / + panel indicator). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-17): A — hard timeout (≈3 s), console warning, no UI change.**
  Source: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence** for the same pack id across sources (bundled wins /
  last wins / first wins). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-17): A — bundled always wins.** Remote packs never override bundled
  core content; implemented via registry order + explicit test. Source:
  worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.

# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),
  `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md`.
- Automated find-related report appended below (if produced).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — external chart library vs Phaser canvas.** Chart.js needs a canvas
  context; overlaying it on the Phaser canvas and keeping it out of
  headless/replay runs needs care. *Mitigation:* isolate the library behind
  `MainStreetStatsChart.ts`, lazy-load/skip in replay/headless, verify bundle
  size.
- **Risk — deferred vs legacy capture paths** could double-record or miss the
  final turn. *Mitigation:* record keyed by `turn` in the shared closing tail,
  with targeted unit tests for both paths.
- **Risk — save/load compatibility.** *Mitigation:* legacy fallback to `[]`,
  with a round-trip + legacy test.
- **Risk — three-column overflow at 1280×720.** *Mitigation:* recompute panel
  width/height and add a browser fit assertion.
- **Assumption — competitive-mode series scope.** In single-player the five
  series describe the run's economy. In competitive mode the shared
  `resourceBank` is seat-scoped during a turn; this brief assumes the graphs
  show the **human seat's** trajectory. *Open question, recorded in the
  Appendix* — the producer may instead want every seat as a separate series.
- **Assumption — "link to a more detailed screen" is satisfied by the third
  column**, per producer Q5; no separate scene is added.
- **Scope-creep risk:** additional stats or chart types beyond the five listed
  (producer Q4 = none) must be raised as separate work items, not folded in.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Correct project?** This item was created in ContextHub (the Worklog
  CLI tool) but describes a Main Street game screen.
  - **Answer (producer): `tce-main-street`.** Source: interactive reply,
    2026-10-16. *Action:* item relocated — created as MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV in
    `tce-main-street`; the mis-filed WL-0MTCMVIPS007AB02 was closed as a
    relocated duplicate.

- **Q2 — Per-turn history tracking.** The save holds only the current-turn
  `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score` snapshot; a full per-turn history must be added
  unless the save already carries one.
  - (A) Add per-turn history tracking, reusing the snapshot mechanism.
    **Recommended.**
  - (B) Use only static current values (no historical graphs).
  - **Answer (producer):** "Doesn't the save game have that snapshot? If not A
    otherwise reuse that mechanism." *Research:* inspected
    `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — the save persists only the **current**
    `weekStart*` snapshot, not a per-turn series; the `EconomyLedger` history
    is per-mutation and not serialised. Therefore **Option A** applies, reusing
    the `weekStart*` snapshot pattern and persisting a new series. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q3 — Chart/graph approach.**
  - (A) Phaser-based line/bar charts (custom `Graphics`). **Recommended** at
    the time of asking (no new dependency).
  - (B) External charting library (e.g. Chart.js).
  - (C) SVG line plots rendered as Phaser textures.
  - **Answer (producer): B** — use an external charting library (overrode the
    recommendation). Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q4 — Additional stats?** Beyond profit/turn, businesses, cash, staff and
  reputation at end of turn.
  - **Answer (producer): No.** Only the five listed stats. Source:
    interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **Q5 — Summary-screen placement / detailed screen.** "Place the cash at end
  of turn on the summary screen and add a link to a more detailed screen" — is
  the Summary column the right place, with a button to a full-page graph view?
  - **Answer (producer): Add a third column.** The detailed graphs live in a
    third column of the Game Over overlay rather than a separate screen.
    Source: interactive reply, 2026-10-16.

- **OPEN QUESTION (competitive-mode series scope).** In competitive mode,
  should the graphs plot (i) only the human seat's trajectory, or (ii) every
  seat as a separate series? *Working assumption: (i) human seat only.* Noted
  for producer confirmation during review; not blocking.

# Add wall-clock bounded-deferral helper with contract tests

## Headline

Add the shared injectable bounded-deferral helper (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock `setTimeout` re-poll, forced completion at `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`, no-clock degradation, stale-scene guard) together with its contract tests — tests written first, tree green at close. Verified end-to-end: unit tests prove wall-clock enforcement, hidden-tab semantics, injectability and single cap source.

## Summary

# Bumping the engine pin to core dev tip breaks the unit suite (phaser window is not defined)

## Problem statement

`npm run build` runs `engine:sync`, which advances the `./core` submodule and
`configs/engine-pin.json` to the core `dev` tip. At the current tip
(`34e0ab6d`, CG-0MVPXFHBZ004LGEB) the unit suite dies at collection time —
23 suites pull in `@ui` (via `src/scenes/…` → `@ui/shakeIllegalMove`), whose
new `illegalMoveToastView` → `Renderer` chain value-imports `phaser`, and
Phaser's device detection touches `window` under node
(`ReferenceError: window is not defined`, `phaser/src/device/OS.js`). A normal
build therefore leaves a red tree that the dev-push pre-push hook refuses, and
the workaround in use pins core behind the tip.

## Users

- **Game developer in this repo** — must be able to `npm run build` and then
  `npm test` on the resulting pin with both green, without manual
  `git -C core checkout …` gymnastics or offline `engine:sync` fallbacks.
- **Dev-push gate / audit** — a green full-suite cache entry must be producible
  at the pinned engine, or no work item can reach `in_review` (`implement.py
  finish` runs the build, which re-pins to the tip).

User stories:

- As a developer, I can run `npm run build` followed by `npm test` on the
  composed pin, and both pass, so I never have to remember the pinned-commit
  workaround.
- As the release line, I can `engine:verify` the recorded pin because the pin
  sha resolves on core `dev`, so release builds are reproducible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — engine checkout consistent:** `npm run engine:check` passes: the
  `./core` checkout equals `configs/engine-pin.json` sha equals the `core`
  gitlink at HEAD; the Vitest root preflight no longer aborts every project
  ("project unit executed 0 of 388 expected file(s)").
- **AC2 — unit suite green at the tip:** with the pin at the current core `dev`
  tip, `npm test` (unit + unit-cli via the test skill) passes with **zero**
  `window is not defined` collection errors, and the full project suite
  (including browser) passes at the new pin.
- **AC3 — no per-file mock shim:** the green result does not come from adding
  `vi.mock('phaser')` / `vi.mock('@ui/…')` to the 23 affected test files purely
  to survive the core import chain; a node-environment regression guard covers
  the affected core import chain (`@ui/shakeIllegalMove` → `illegalMoveToastView`
  / `Renderer`) — either this repo's guard or the engine-side guard from
  CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ.
- **AC4 — pin movement attributable:** the re-pin (`core` gitlink advance +
  `configs/engine-pin.json` sha change, both staged together) is its own commit
  whose message names this item and the engine commit consumed; no feature work
  is mixed in.
- **AC5 — documentation:** all related documentation and code comments are
  updated — `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (pin policy, offline fallback),
  `docs/dev/testing.md` (engine-checkout preflight), any workaround notes in
  commit messages/comments describing the 0409c1eb hold — to reflect the new
  pin and the removed workaround.

## Constraints

- **Engine-side fix is upstream, not here.** The `@ui` barrel change belongs to
  the core repo and is already tracked: CG-0MVQQ2M8E003FQMZ (open). This item
  must not duplicate that code change inside `./core`; it consumes it via
  re-pin. The one allowed local alternative, if the producer elects it at
  review, is a node-safe Phaser stub alias scoped to the `unit`/`unit-cli`
  Vitest projects only (see Desired change §4) — acceptable but inferior
  because it fixes only this repo.
- **Pin + gitlink travel together** (CG-0MVO268500071BPI): one actor, one
  moment, one commit — a re-pin commit can never record them divergent, and the
  offline `engine:sync` fallback must NOT be used for this transition (it would
  silently keep the stale pin).
- **Push policy:** dev only. **Implement worktree requirement** applies at
  implementation time (`implement.py start/finish`, worktree isolation,
  hygiene checks).
- **Repository boundaries:** no edits to `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` trees.

## Existing state

- Pin held at `0409c1eb`; MS-0MVPWS6WB008WP79 (takeLoan) shipped with the
  workaround: core kept at `0409c1eb` and `engine:sync` forced into its
  documented offline fallback so the pin cannot drift; the blocker id is
  recorded in that commit's work-item comment.
- Second symptom (Map, MS-C0MVQPA5BZ002NIH5): the main checkout's `./core`
  clone could not resolve the pinned commit at all (clone HEAD `7afa0014`, pin
  `0409c1eb` absent), so the Vitest preflight aborted every project before a
  single test ran. During this intake the clone was fetched
  (`git -C core fetch origin --prune`), which brought `0409c1eb` and
  `34e0ab6d` in; the working tree still shows `M core` (checkout `7afa0014` ≠
  gitlink `0409c1eb`), so `engine:check` stays red until `engine:sync` advances
  the checkout and pin together.
- 22 test files already `vi.mock('phaser', () => ({ default: {} }))` for
  *active* Phaser use — those are fine and unaffected; the 23 failing suites
  are exactly the ones whose graph reaches `@ui` without a barrel mock.
- Root-cause chain confirmed against core `34e0ab6d`:
  `shakeIllegalMove.ts` → `illegalMoveToastView.ts` → `Renderer/index.ts`

  usage is type-only.

## Desired change

## Risks & assumptions

# Verification: remote pack discovery, integrity & degradation

## Goal

Prove — with automated tests — that a remote pack catalogue is discovered,
cryptographically verified, and safely degraded when anything goes wrong, so
the parent's discovery, degradation, rejection and integrity criteria are
met by evidence rather than assertion.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1, 3, 4 and 6).

## Scope

Verification-only: this item adds or hardens tests and fixtures; it does not
add production behaviour. Where a test exposes a real gap in the remote
source, record the gap and raise a comment on the sibling feature item rather
than implementing the fix here.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Discovery.** A pack catalogue served from a configured host appears in
   the discovery result alongside bundled packs, with its manifest, cards CSV
   and pack id intact.
2. **Signature gate.** A valid signature loads; missing, invalid, wrong-key,
   and malformed-envelope manifests each reject the source **whole** (every
   path from that source resolves `null`) with exactly one warning.
3. **Degradation.** Unreachable host, connection rejection, HTTP error,
   slow/hung host (bounded timeout), and malformed manifest JSON each leave
   boot on bundled content, never throw, and never leave the Card Packs
   listing empty when a bundled pack exists.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A pack whose CSV header is wrong, or whose card
   ids duplicate an already-accepted pack, is rejected by the existing core
   merge without affecting packs from other sources.

Tests must use an injected fake `fetch`/transport and injected timers so the
suite never performs real network I/O and never waits a real 3 seconds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Remote discovery is covered: a signed remote pack served by a fake
      transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks`' result with its cards
      merged into the pool.
- [ ] Every signature failure mode is covered: missing signature, invalid
      signature, signature from a non-pinned key, and malformed envelope each
      reject the whole source and emit exactly one warning.
- [ ] Every degradation mode is covered: unreachable host, rejected fetch,
      non-2xx response, timeout abort, and unparseable manifest each boot on
      bundled content with no throw.
- [ ] A test asserts the timeout is bounded at the configured value using fake
      timers — no test waits on a real clock.
- [ ] A test asserts the Card Packs listing input is non-empty when a bundled
      pack exists and the remote source fails.
- [ ] Bad pack data (wrong header, duplicate card ids) is covered as rejected
      whole without affecting sibling sources.
- [ ] No test performs real network I/O; every fetch goes through an injected
      transport.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass through the test skill.

## Key Files

- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDiscovery.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackIntegrity.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDegradation.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/remotePackFixtures.ts`
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts`

## Deliverables

- Automated tests covering discovery, integrity and degradation.
- A reusable signed-manifest fixture helper (keypair generation, signing,
  tampering, fake transport) consumed by the sibling verification item.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.
- Depends on *Remote pack degradation & bounded timeout hardening*.

# Verification: remote pack precedence, gating & asset parity

## Goal

Prove that remote packs are indistinguishable from bundled packs at the
registry, gating and asset layers, and that precedence is deterministic, so the
parent's parity, precedence and asset-resolution criteria are evidenced by
automated tests.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2, 5 and 7).

## Scope

Verification-only: this item adds tests and fixtures; it does not add
production behaviour. Gaps found are reported on the sibling feature items.

Coverage to establish:

1. **Precedence — bundled wins.** A pack id present in both the bundled and a
   remote source is served from the bundled source, byte-for-byte.
2. **Precedence — remote first-wins.** Two remote sources carrying the same
   pack id resolve to the first-registered source's content.
3. **Registry composition.** The composed registry order is bundled first,
   then remote sources in configured URL order; registration is idempotent by
   id and never reorders existing sources.
4. **Gating parity.** An entitled remote pack is loaded; an unentitled remote
   pack is `locked` and contributes no rows; the scoped simulated purchase
   promotes the declared remote pack and re-discovers it — the same flow as
   the bundled residential pack.
5. **Persistence parity.** A save created with a remote pack active restores
   the same active pack set and merged checksum after a load round-trip.
6. **Asset parity.** A remote pack's `assetUrls` entries resolve to absolute
   URLs on the configured remote base, are gated on manifest verification, and
   reject traversal/undeclared asset paths.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test asserts bundled content wins over a remote source carrying the
      same pack id (byte-for-byte comparison).
- [ ] A test asserts first-wins between two remote sources in registration
      order.
- [ ] A test asserts the composed registry order is bundled → remote(s) in
      configured order, and that re-adding a source is a no-op.
- [ ] A test asserts an unentitled remote pack is reported `locked` and

- [ ] A test asserts the scoped simulated purchase unlocks the declared remote

- [ ] A save/load round-trip test asserts the active remote pack set and merged
      checksum are preserved.
- [ ] A test asserts remote `assetUrls` resolve to the configured remote base,

      traversal asset paths resolve `null`.
- [ ] Changed-scope tests pass through the test skill.

# Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a signed pack catalogue hosted at a
configured URL to be discovered at runtime and merged into the player's card
pool, so that I can publish packs without rebuilding the game; as a player I
want those packs to show up in my Card Packs panel exactly like bundled packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 1 and 6; parent scope items 1, 2, 6;
parent constraints "reuse existing seams", "totality", "additive", "signing key
separation"; locked decisions Q1 and Q2).

## Context

This is the tracer bullet: it cuts every layer once, end-to-end, so the whole
seam is proven before it is hardened. `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` already provides
`PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry` and adapts a registry to the loader's
`fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` seams, so **no core loader change**
is needed. The remote source is a provider on that registry.

Without this slice there is no usable increment: a signature gate is
inseparable from discovery (an unverified catalogue must never contribute
packs), so verification lands with the first end-to-end path rather than as a
separate layer.

## Scope

1. **Configuration surface.** Read the remote catalogue coordinates from
   `import.meta.env` (`VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL`,
   `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`), validate them, and derive the host
   allow-list. Inert when unset.
2. **Allow-listed bounded fetch primitive.** One total text-fetch helper: refuse
   a host that is not configured (before any request), enforce a hard timeout
   via `AbortController`, map every failure to `null` + one warning.
3. **Signed-manifest verification.** The signed envelope, its deterministic
   canonical payload bytes, pinned-key import from raw base64, and a total
   verifier returning a discriminated result (never throws).
4. **Remote pack source.** `createRemotePackSource(config)` serving
   `<base>/packs/manifest.json` and `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`
   after verification, rejecting the **whole source** on any verification or
   manifest-shape failure.
5. **Composition and boot wiring.** Compose the registry as bundled source
   first, then the remote source; use it on the browser boot path
   (`bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks`) without touching the Electron
   content-directory path.

## Design notes

- Ed25519 is available natively in Node 22 WebCrypto and the Playwright
  Chromium used by the browser project — **no new runtime dependency**.
- Verification is memoised per source instance: one manifest fetch and one
  verification per boot, not one per CSV.
- The source's remit is "fetch and refuse only". Merging, precedence and
  duplicate-id rejection stay with the registry and the core merge, which is
  what makes bundled/remote parity automatic.
- Every failure is a warning on the existing logger seam; no UI change
  (decision Q3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` parses and validates `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY` (injectable env for tests) and exposes an allow-list predicate; unset, blank or invalid configuration yields no remote sources and logs a warning rather than throwing.
- [ ] `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` exports the signed envelope type and a deterministic canonical-payload function, plus `verifyPackManifestSignature(...)` returning `ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` / `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable` and never throwing for any input.
- [ ] A manifest signed with the matching private key verifies `ok`; a one-byte body change or a signature from a different keypair returns `invalid-signature`; a blank or absent signature returns `missing-signature`; a non-JSON or wrong-shape envelope returns `malformed-envelope`.
- [ ] The canonical payload is stable under input key reordering so an external operator can reproduce the signed bytes; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A total fetched-text helper refuses a non-configured host **without calling the injected `fetch`**, and maps timeout, rejection, non-2xx and body-read failure to `null` with one warning.
- [ ] A `createRemotePackSource(config)` factory returns a `PackSource` whose `id` distinguishes it from the bundled source, serving `manifest.json` and `<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv` from the configured base once the manifest verifies.
- [ ] A remote pack served by a fake transport appears in `loadMainStreetCardPacks` merged pool with its cards and reaches the Card Packs listing input; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A missing, invalid, non-pinned-key or malformed manifest makes **every** path from that source resolve `null`, logs exactly one source-level warning, and never throws.
- [ ] The remote source never throws for any input (invalid config, non-string path, empty path, throwing transport), asserted by a table-driven test.
- [ ] `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` composes the configured remote source on the browser path, while an explicit launcher `contentDir` composes no remote source and performs no remote fetch (asserted with a spy).
- [ ] No new entry is added to `package.json` dependencies.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRemotePackConfig.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackManifest.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetRemotePackFetch.ts` (new)
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, composition
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — boot wiring on the browser path
- `./env.d.ts` — declared env vars
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDiscovery.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackIntegrity.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/fixtures/remotePackFixtures.ts`

## Deliverables

- The end-to-end discovery path: configured URL → verified manifest → served
  CSV → merged pool → listing.
- The configuration, verifier and fetch primitives the later slices harden.
- Signed-manifest fixtures (keypair generation, signing, tampering, fake
  transport) reused by the verification items.

## Dependencies

None — this is the first slice.

# Remote pack degradation & bounded timeout hardening

## Goal

As a player, I want the game to always start and play on bundled packs when the
remote host is slow, hung, unreachable or serving rubbish, so that remote
hosting can never block boot or leave me with an empty Card Packs panel.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 3 and 4; parent scope items 5 and 7;
parent constraint "bounded timeout"; locked decision Q3).

## Context

The tracer bullet proves the happy path. This slice hardens the failure paths,
which is where the parent's risk register concentrates (boot latency, offline
regression). All of it is end-to-end observable: the game boots, bundled cards
deal, the listing is non-empty, and the console shows exactly one actionable
warning per rejected source.

## Scope

- Enforce the hard ≈3 s timeout on **every** remote request (manifest and each
  pack CSV), with the abort timer always cleared so no handle leaks.
- Degrade to bundled content — never throw, never blank the listing — for:
  unreachable host, connection rejection, non-2xx status, timeout abort,
  unparseable manifest JSON, wrong manifest schema/version, and a manifest
  entry with no readable `cards` file.
- Per-pack isolation: one unreadable CSV degrades only that pack, so other
  packs from the same source still load.
- Explicit "no client-side caching" behaviour: the source writes nothing to
  `localStorage` / Cache Storage and re-fetches on each boot.
- Warning quality: one warning per rejected source and one per failed pack,
  naming the source/pack and the reason.

## Design notes

- The timeout is per request, so a hung manifest does not consume the budget of
  every CSV read.
- Tests use injected `fetch` and fake timers throughout: no real network, no
  real 3-second waits.
- The bounded-timeout default (3000 ms) is a single exported constant so the
  documentation and the tests reference one value.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
- [ ] A hard timeout (default 3000 ms, exported constant, overridable) is applied to every remote request and abort is enforced with `AbortController`; a fake-timer test asserts the default value and that a hung request resolves `null` at the deadline.
- [ ] The abort timer is cleared on every path (success, error, timeout), asserted with fake timers and a settled request so no dangling handle remains.
- [ ] An unreachable host, a rejected `fetch`, a non-2xx response, a timeout and an unparseable manifest each complete boot on bundled content with exactly one warning and no throw.
- [ ] A manifest with an unexpected schema or version, or listing a pack whose `cards` file is missing, is rejected whole with one warning.
- [ ] A single unreadable CSV resolves `null` for that pack only; another pack CSV from the same source still resolves and its cards still merge.
- [ ] A pack whose CSV header is wrong, or whose card ids duplicate an already-accepted pack, is rejected without affecting packs from other sources.
- [ ] The Card Packs listing input is non-empty when a bundled pack exists and the remote source fails (asserted by a test).
- [ ] A test asserts the remote path performs no `localStorage` or Cache Storage writes (no client-side caching this iteration).
- [ ] Warnings name the offending source and/or pack and the failure reason; asserted for each failure mode.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetRemotePackFetch.ts`
- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackDegradation.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Bounded, leak-free timeout enforcement across every remote request.
- Total degradation across all availability and data-quality failure modes,
  with actionable warnings.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.

# Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack to never override bundled core content, and
deterministic behaviour when two remote catalogues offer the same pack, so that
remote hosting cannot silently replace or corrupt the game's own packs.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 5; parent scope items 2 and 3; parent
constraint "additive"; locked decision Q4).

## Context

`PackSourceRegistry` is first-wins by consultation order and `add()` never
reorders. Precedence is therefore *derived from composition order*. The tracer
bullet composed one remote source; this slice makes composition a first-class,
explicitly ordered function that supports several remote catalogues, and pins
the precedence guarantees with tests.

Equally important: the change must remain **inert** for the Electron
content-directory path and for an unconfigured build.

## Scope

- Compose several remote sources additively in configured URL order, always
  after the bundled source.
- Guarantee and test: bundled wins over remote (byte-for-byte); between remote
  sources the first registered wins.
- Idempotent, order-preserving composition; re-adding a duplicate source id is a
  no-op.
- Resilience: a remote source that cannot be constructed is skipped with a
  warning; bundled content still serves.
- Inertness: configuration unset, and the Electron content-directory path, both
  behave exactly as before (no remote source, no remote fetch).
- Gating is untouched — remote packs flow through the unchanged
  `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` resolver, so nothing is automatically
  ungated.

## Design notes

- Composition is a distinct, explicitly named entry point beside
  `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry`; the latter keeps its bundled-only meaning
  so existing callers and tests are unaffected.
- One place decides source order, mirroring the module's existing contract that
  "the registry is the single place source order is decided".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
- [ ] A composition function (e.g. `createConfiguredPackSourceRegistry(config)`) returns a registry whose `sources` order is exactly the bundled source followed by each configured remote source in configured URL order.
- [ ] `createDefaultPackSourceRegistry()` remains bundled-only; existing registry behaviour and tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] A test asserts bundled content wins when the bundled and a remote source both carry the same pack path (byte-for-byte comparison).
- [ ] A test asserts a pack id offered by two remote sources resolves to the first-registered source content.
- [ ] Composition is idempotent: composing twice, or adding a source with a duplicate id, creates no duplicate and reorders nothing.
- [ ] A remote source that throws during construction is skipped with a warning and the bundled source still serves content.
- [ ] With configuration unset, the browser boot path yields a result identical to the bundled-only build.
- [ ] With an explicit launcher `contentDir`, no remote source is composed and no remote fetch occurs (asserted with a spy `fetch`).
- [ ] A remote pack cards reach the applied pool through `bootstrapMainStreetCardPacks` when configured.
- [ ] An unentitled remote pack is reported `locked`; no ungating shortcut is introduced.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts`
- `src/createMainStreetGame.ts`
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackPrecedence.test.ts`
- `tests/main-street/PackSourceRegistry.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Ordered, multi-source composition with explicit precedence guarantees.
- Tests for precedence, idempotence, resilience and inertness.

# Remote pack asset resolution

## Goal

As a player, I want a remote pack's card art to render correctly, so that a
remote pack looks and plays exactly like a bundled pack.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 7; parent scope item 1; related work
`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` — pack assets self-contained).

## Context

`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` made pack art travel with the pack: the loader produces
`tce-packs://` asset URLs, `resolvePackFileUrl` maps them through the registry,
and pack art is registered from `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`. A bundled source
answers with a same-origin Vite `?url`; a remote source must answer with an
absolute URL on the configured remote base, and only for assets the verified
manifest declares.

This is a vertical slice: registry resolution → loader `assetUrls` → the pack
art registry → the rendered card texture.

## Scope

- Implement `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` on the remote source, returning
  `<base>/packs/<path>` for assets declared by the verified manifest.
- Gate resolution on successful manifest verification: a rejected source
  resolves no assets.
- Reject paths that escape the packs root (traversal) or are not declared by the
  manifest.
- Verify the resolved URL reaches `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` and the pack art
  registry so a remote pack's art is available before textures are generated.

## Design notes

- URL joining must respect a base URL with a path component (a catalogue may be
  hosted under a prefix) and must not double or drop slashes.
- The source returns a URL only; the existing asset-byte transport performs the
  fetch, so the remote source adds no new byte-reading path.
- No caching of asset URLs across boots (consistent with "no client-side
  caching this iteration").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
- [ ] The remote source implements `resolvePackFileUrl(path)` returning an absolute URL on the configured remote base for an asset declared by the verified manifest.
- [ ] A base URL carrying a path prefix (e.g. `https://host/packs-v2/`) is joined correctly; asserted by a test.
- [ ] A rejected source (failed signature or malformed manifest) resolves no asset URLs.
- [ ] An asset path not declared in the manifest, and a path containing `..` or a backslash traversal, resolves `null`.
- [ ] An integration test asserts a remote pack `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` entry is the remote absolute URL and that pack art registration receives it.
- [ ] A remote pack with art renders in the browser pack path, covered by an asset-resolution assertion or a browser test.
- [ ] The source does not add a new asset byte-read path; the existing `fetchAsset` transport still performs the read.

## Key Files

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `resolvePackFileUrl` on the remote source
- `src/MainStreetCardPackArt.ts` — pack art registration seam
- `tests/main-street/RemotePackAssets.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Remote asset URL resolution gated on manifest verification.
- Tests covering URL shape, prefix joining, gating and traversal rejection.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.

# Remote pack gating & behaviour parity

## Goal

As a player, I want remote packs to lock, purchase, enable, deal and persist
exactly like bundled packs, so that hosting a pack remotely changes where it
comes from and nothing else.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent ACs 2 and 4; parent scope item 4).

## Context

Content-unlock gating is data-driven: `MAIN_STREET_CONTENT_UNLOCK_GATED_PACKS`
declares which packs are gated and `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` plugs into
the loader's `resolveEntitlement` seam. Remote packs must flow through that same
resolver unchanged — the remote source contributes *content*, never
*entitlement*. This slice proves that and covers the interactive flow end to
end.

## Scope

- Confirm an entitled remote pack loads and its cards merge; an unentitled
  remote pack is `locked` and contributes no rows.
- Confirm the scoped simulated purchase (`purchaseMainStreetCardPack`) unlocks a
  declared remote pack, re-discovers it with the same transports, and that the
  pack's cards then merge and deal.
- Confirm enable/disable parity (`applyEnabledMainStreetPacks`), including the
  refusal when a live card instance would be stranded.
- Confirm save/load round-trip parity: the active remote pack set and merged
  checksum are persisted and restored.
- Introduce no ungating shortcut: the remote source must not bypass or relax
  `resolveEntitlement`.

## Design notes

- The pack id a remote catalogue publishes is the entitlement key, exactly as
  for a bundled pack (`dlc:<gameId>:<packId>`). A remote pack that is not
  declared in the gating table keeps the default (Steam-DLC / declared-unlock)
  behaviour — it is never implicitly free.
- This slice is test-and-wiring only where the parity already holds; any real
  gap found becomes a fix here because parity is the parent's AC2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
- [ ] A test asserts an entitled remote pack is loaded by `loadMainStreetCardPacks` and its cards appear in the merged pool.
- [ ] A test asserts an unentitled remote pack is reported in `locked` and contributes zero merged rows.
- [ ] A test asserts `purchaseMainStreetCardPack` unlocks a declared remote pack, re-discovers it, and returns `purchased: true`, with the pack cards merged afterwards.
- [ ] A test asserts the scoped purchase evaluates only the declared pack purchase rule (no collateral unlocks).
- [ ] A test asserts a save/load round-trip preserves the remote pack active set (id plus version) and merged checksum.
- [ ] A test asserts enabling and disabling a remote pack re-merges the pool, and that disabling is refused while one of its cards is live in state.
- [ ] A test asserts the remote source never supplies or overrides an entitlement; gating remains owned by `composeContentUnlockEntitlement`.
- [ ] The full pack flow (lock, purchase, enable, deal) is covered for a remote pack by automated tests.

- `src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts`
- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`

# Documentation: remote pack hosting contract

## Goal

As a distribution operator, I want a written contract for hosting a remote pack
catalogue — where the files go, how the manifest is signed, what the game does
when it cannot verify or reach the host — so that I can publish packs without
reading the source code.

Child of `MS-0MV26X8T200852AC` (parent AC 8, parent scope item 8).

## Scope

- **Configuration** — `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`,
  that they are build-time (changing a URL requires a rebuild), and that
  multiple URLs compose in order.
- **Hosting layout** — the exact URL paths the game requests:
  `<base>/packs/manifest.json`, `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/cards.csv`,
  `<base>/packs/<gameId>/<packId>/assets/…`. A worked example tree is required.
- **Signing contract** — the signed envelope shape, the canonical payload bytes
  (including key ordering and whitespace rules), the algorithm (Ed25519) and
  the key separation rule: the private key is held by the operator and never
  shipped in the game. Include a worked example and the verification outcome
  table.
- **Degradation semantics** — the ≈3 s bounded timeout, console-warning-only
  degradation, bundled-wins precedence, no client-side caching, and that
  bundled packs remain the offline story.
- **Licence-clean requirement** — remote pack content must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs.

## Design notes

- Documentation-only slice: it consumes the contract implemented by the
  sibling feature items and must not introduce new behaviour.
- The verification outcome table must match the verifier's discriminated
  results exactly (`ok` / `missing-signature` / `invalid-signature` /
  `malformed-envelope` / `unavailable`), so operators can map a console warning
  to a cause.
- Explicitly list the recorded follow-ups (signing tooling, client-side
  caching, runtime/launcher URL configuration) so operators know what is not
  in this iteration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Parent AC (owned): **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
- [ ] `packs/README.md` documents the remote catalogue layout with a worked URL tree, and states that a hosted catalogue uses the same `manifest.json` shape as the bundled packs plus the signature.
- [ ] The signed-envelope shape and canonical payload rules are documented with a worked example an operator can reproduce, and every verifier failure reason is listed with its meaning.
- [ ] `./DEPLOYMENT.md` (or a linked page under `docs/`) documents `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` and `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_PUBLIC_KEY`, the rebuild-to-change rule, and multiple-URL ordering.
- [ ] Degradation semantics are documented: about 3 s timeout, console warning only, bundled always wins, no UI change, no client-side caching.
- [ ] The signing key separation rule is stated: the private key never ships; only the public key is pinned at build time.
- [ ] The licence-clean requirement for remote pack content is stated.
- [ ] The out-of-scope follow-ups (signing tooling, caching, runtime URL configuration) are recorded as follow-ups, not documented as available.
- [ ] Existing documentation tests still pass and the new sections are reachable from the README.

## Key Files

- `packs/README.md`
- `./DEPLOYMENT.md`
- `./README.md`
- `docs/index.md`

## Deliverables

- The hosting contract documentation for distribution operators.
- A verification-outcome table mapping warnings to causes.

## Dependencies

- Depends on *Remote pack discovery end-to-end (tracer bullet)*.
- Depends on *Multi-source composition & deterministic precedence*.
- Depends on *Remote pack asset resolution*.


Critical path: **F1 → F3 → F5 → V2 → V3**.

Verification items are created first and depend on the features they verify —
the same shape as the sibling work under `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`
(`MS-0MV53CEUR0097K0H`, `MS-0MV53CF6O007J2UY`, `MS-0MV53CFIN003F6U4`).

## Vertical-slice rationale

An earlier draft split this into layers (config / crypto / fetch / source /
composition). That was rejected during the sequencing review: layer phases are
not independently deliverable and would have left four items with no
user-observable outcome. The final phasing is tracer-bullet vertical:

- **F1** cuts every layer once (config → allow-listed bounded fetch → Ed25519
  verification → remote source → registry composition → boot → merged pool →
  listing). The signature gate is deliberately inside the tracer bullet: an
  unverified catalogue must never contribute packs, so verification is
  inseparable from discovery.
- **F2–F5** each harden one user-observable property end-to-end across all
  layers (degradation, precedence, art, gating/persistence), each with its own
  tests and console observability.
- Every feature item's ACs include its own automated tests, and the three
  verification items provide the independent evidence layer.

## Traceability (no duplicate work)

`wl search "remote pack source bundle"` → the only related items are already
completed dependencies or context, not duplicates:
`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` (registry seam, completed),
`MS-0MV53CFUS004DFX1` (bundled source, completed),
`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (self-contained pack assets, completed),
`MS-0MV53CH78004I2BF` (browser pack docs, completed).

No child was closed as a duplicate and no child AC is already satisfied by a
completed item: all of the above file remote-hosting as explicitly out of
scope.

## Reuse identified

- `PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry` and `createPackSourceTransports`
  (`src/MainStreetPackSources.ts`) — no core loader change.
- `composeContentUnlockEntitlement` (`src/MainStreetContentUnlockGate.ts`) —
  gating reused unchanged, so no ungating shortcut is possible.
- `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` seam (`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`) for remote art.
- `computeMergedChecksum` / `mergeCardPackCsv` for duplicate-id rejection and
  save/load parity — reused, not reimplemented.

## Assumptions recorded (not producer questions)

These resolve the effort/risk report's open unknowns; none changes producer
intent, so none was raised as a blocking question.

- **A1 — Ed25519 mechanism.** WebCrypto `crypto.subtle` Ed25519 with the raw
  32-byte public key. Verified available in this environment: Node v22.22.1
  (generate/sign/verify/export round-trip) and Playwright 1.64.1's Chromium for
  the browser project. **No new runtime dependency.** Where Ed25519 is

  the safe-refusal behaviour AC 6 already requires.

  32-byte Ed25519 key), both build-time. This follows the intake brief's own

- 2026-10-28 — Plan skill run (`plan`). Created 9 children (3 task, 5 feature,

  child after the AC coverage review first returned `stop` on lexical matching.

**No producer questions were asked in this session.** The intake brief already
carried four producer-locked decisions, so re-asking them would have violated
the interview contract. The plan-level unknowns the effort/risk report listed
were resolved by research in this session and are recorded above as
assumptions A1–A5.

  setting / well-known URL). **Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-17): A — build-time config constant.** Final: yes, build-time.
  Carried forward into F1 and D1. Evidence: worklog comment
  `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`; restated in assumption A2.
- **Q (intake, Q2) — Pack-integrity model** (allow-list / allow-list + checksum
  / signed manifests). **Answer (producer, interactive reply, 2026-10-17):
  C — signed manifests (Ed25519).** Final: yes, Ed25519 signed manifests.
  Carried forward into F1. Evidence: worklog comment `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.
- **Q (intake, Q3) — Timeout and degradation behaviour** (hard timeout +

  Final: yes. Carried forward into F2. Evidence: worklog comment

- **Q (intake, Q4) — Merge precedence** for the same pack id across sources
  (bundled wins / last wins / first wins). **Answer (producer, interactive
  reply, 2026-10-17): A — bundled always wins.** Final: yes. Carried forward
  into F3 with an explicit byte-for-byte test. Evidence: worklog comment
  `MS-C0MVC8TJJA0030X19`.

  browser test project, and does it need a dependency?** Resolved by research:
  WebCrypto Ed25519 round-trips in Node v22.22.1 (signature 64 bytes, raw

Both are injectable (`now`/`schedule`/`clear`) and default to the real wall clock; a host with no timers falls back to the scene-clock poll alone. Semantics are identical at every deferral site: resolve on flag-clear (fast path), force at the cap, exactly once.
